Final Fantasy

Warrior of Light

Defensive all-rounder with HP links, solid from every angle

Fastest BRV 13F (Dayflash ground)Fastest HP 51F (Shining Wave)Dash 77 (Average / Good)ATK 110DEF 1131-hit HP YesMultipleHP links Yes

Standing in the meta

Tier A 14th of 30 — 2017 tournament tier list from dissidia.wiki (half matchup values, half expert player votes).

Ranked 14th (tier A) on the 2017 tier list: a consistent high tier, carried by a fundamentally solid moveset that fits the metagame.

Overview

The Warrior of Light is a versatile melee fighter who does everything competently. His style rests on classic fundamentals: fast pokes with Dayflash, committal gap closers, mid-range projectiles. His standard mobility lets him build offence as well as defence, and as soon as an opening appears, his HP links deal good damage, supported by high base bravery builds, HP Wall Rush and assist combos; he works with a great many assists and his combo routes stay consistent almost everywhere. The coverage of his HP links (Shield Strike / Rising Buckler > Bitter End) lets him punish from almost every angle.

His standout assets are defensive: a very high base DEF (113, among the best), amplified further in EX Mode (+10), and above all Shield of Light, an advancing command block that guards from frame 1 and finishes with a 1-hit HP attack carrying Wall Rush — a rare property in this game. That option makes his dodges safe and beats low-priority attacks with long active frames. As an all-rounder, he accommodates a wide variety of builds, including EX and Side by Side.

His limits: he struggles against persistent projectiles, his disjoints being risky, and his own projectiles remain decent but offer little return at range. His reliance on HP links exposes him to punishes after an LV1 Assist Change; safer options exist, at the cost of damage. His air dodge has an average fall speed ratio, which he sometimes has to cover with Shield of Light — a powerful but highly committal option, and a vulnerable one when it fails.

Competitively, the Warrior of Light is usually ranked high tier: a fundamentally good moveset and stats, for a consistent style in tune with the metagame.

Strengths

  • All-rounder: average to good stats, HP links and a moveset with an answer to most situations.
  • Accessible: excellent for beginners and seasoned players alike, ideal for learning the game and working on fundamentals.
  • Command block: Shield of Light, an advancing 1-hit HP attack that guards instantly throughout its startup, useful on offence as well as after a dodge.
  • Ground game: projectiles and assist combo starters through empty chases, to adapt the pace of the match.
  • Build synergy: works with every common style, including EX, bravery boost on dodge and Side by Side.
  • EX generation: most of his bravery attacks produce 30 to 90 EX Force; Dayflash, his main poke, generates 90.
  • EX Mode: the highest DEF in the game, automatic blocking of Ranged Low projectiles and increased damage on his melee bravery attacks.

Weaknesses

  • Struggles against traps: for all his projectiles and disjoints, he cannot easily punish characters sheltering behind persistent projectiles without spending resources or taking significant risk.
  • Committal vertical attacks: Rising Buckler and Shield Strike are decent but reactable and impossible to cancel early on whiff.
  • The 4 bravery slot dilemma: all his aerial bravery attacks are useful to him, but he cannot equip them all.
  • A floaty air dodge and risky protection: Shield of Light covers his aerial dodges well, but the option is very risky and loses to high-priority attacks; outside a Dayflash clash, his air dodges leave him vulnerable.

Aerial

Crossover 23FMelee Low

An advancing bravery attack with an HP link, the aerial alternative to Ascension: it punishes long attacks and staggered opponents, and can be used to approach sparingly. HP attacks

Ground

Shield of Light (ground) 53F (Block from 1F to 53F)Melee High, Block Mid

His signature command block: he advances then releases a 1-hit blast that Wall Rushes, guarding from frame 1 until the hit. It punishes low-priority pokes and serves as immediate defence after a ground dodge. It only blocks low priorities — HP attacks and higher moves guard crush or stagger him — and a miss leaves him wide open. It becomes airborne in use and automatically aims diagonally at an airborne opponent, with no correction possible along the way.

Shining Wave 51FMelee High (blade) Ranged High (light pillar)

A long-range HP attack in the form of a wave: a counter-attack after a block stagger and passive space control. A solid anti-air (instant high vertical hitboxes, full rotation), with beams that cannot be reflected and persist even when blocked, and Ranged High priority that ignores LV2 Assist Change staggers in a combo. To be used sparingly: he is vulnerable after the shot, it loses to high-priority melee and to Jecht's and Exdeath's command blocks, and it can miss against very fast movement through the projectile.

Ultimate Shield 41FMelee High

His fastest ground HP attack (41F), for punishing blocks, close dodges and even attacks, with strong hemispherical tracking. He stays in place while the shield goes out; without contact there is no combo follow-up, hence a little more safety at range. It reflects HP projectiles without advancing. A hit glitch with White Fang can trigger the follow-ups without contact, which can cost dearly; long recovery, so beware of Assist Changes.

EX Mode: Class Change! & EX Burst

The “Class Change!” EX Mode — effects: Regen, Critical Boost, Mirror Attack, Protect and Light's Blessing. The Warrior of Light gains extra hits on his melee bravery attacks (Light's Blessing, swords of light at 1 base damage each, a source of hit stun without new solo combo routes), a large damage reduction through +10 base DEF (Protect) and the blocking of Ranged Low attacks during his attack animations, recovery included (Mirror Attack).

Since EX Modes mostly serve to secure a win through an assist combo, the defensive bonuses rarely come fully into play — assists often interrupt EX Mode and the opponent can run away to buy time if the Warrior of Light does not lock them into a combo. It remains a competent EX Mode.

EX Burst : Oversoul is a fairly standard EX Burst: six directional inputs to enter correctly (the analogue stick is refused), near-immediate follow-ups that leave the opponent little time to raise their DEF and, whatever the outcome, a final strike at 25 base damage.

Gameplan & advanced tech

The gameplay loop is built around Dayflash: whiff the poke without risk to fill the assist gauge, generate 90 EX per hit and confirm hits visually to go into an assist combo. On the ground, White Fang covers the approach and links into Ascension (White Fang > Ascension > Rune Saber, his reference solo route: 56 minimum plus HP damage and Wall Rush) or into Dayflash with a delayed empty chase to force a ground Wall Rush, pick up all the EX on the stage and call another assist.

HP damage comes through three channels: the HP links (Ascension/Crossover > Rune Saber, Rising Buckler/Shield Strike > Bitter End), which punish without an assist from almost every angle; assist combos started off Dayflash or a Wall Rush (typical midscreen combo: Dayflash 2 hits > BRV assist > Assist Chase > Shield Strike > Bitter End); and Shield of Light as a defensive read, which turns a block into a Wall Rush.

Defensively, play the double layer: dodge then an instant Shield of Light against dashes and low-priority attacks — the opponent risks HP damage simply by approaching. Keep that highly committal option for the moments that need it, though: it loses to high priorities and leaves him wide open on a miss.

On resources, Dayflash's EX generation supports long-term survival through the EX gauge, and high base bravery builds maximise the bravery returned during Bitter End's long animations at the end of an assist combo. Finally, mind the reliance on HP links: after an opponent's LV1 Assist Change, Bitter End and Rune Saber become punishable — favour the safe options over damage then.

Character-specific tech

Dayflash empty chase reset

Delay Dayflash's Chase as long as possible, then trigger it just before the opponent touches the ground to force a Wall Rush reaction. It allows him to chase without being countered, to recover all the EX on the stage and to reset his assist usage so as to extend a combo if another bar is in stock. The community record of empty chases confirms Dayflash (on the ground) among the rare moves in the cast that offer this reset.

Sources: pastebin.com/dKSWgUQ6

Bitter End knockback cancel

Press the assist (Sephiroth) at the exact moment Bitter End's last bravery hit connects: the assist strikes during the end of the animation and holds the opponent in place, opening a second Shield Strike > Bitter End anywhere on the stage, with no wall.

Ultimate Shield hit glitch

If White Fang connects at the moment Ultimate Shield is launched, the move chains its follow-ups without any real contact with the opponent. Given the move's short range, this glitch is a trap to know about rather than a tool.

Aerith double assist

After a Wall Rush, Shield of Light can set up a second Aerith assist within the same combo; with high base bravery, the double assist deals very heavy damage.

Documented solo combo routes

White Fang and Blue Fang link into any melee attack except Shield of Light; EX Crossover (without the last hit) > dodge cancel > aerial EX Dayflash; the author also mentions ground EX Dayflash (2 hits on an airborne opponent) > DC > landing lag > EX Crossover, flagging it himself as unconfirmed.

Sources: pastebin.com/8FWDXjvJ

Matchups

The wiki's matchups page is a stub: no detailed table is documented. The sources give a few markers: Rising Buckler gains value in air-oriented matchups such as Sephiroth and Kuja; Blue Fang dislodges characters entrenched behind their projectiles, such as Laguna under Electro Shield or Ultimecia under a charged Knight's Lance; and characters with persistent projectiles remain his main difficulty. Note also that Crossover's last hit can miss at the ceiling against large frames (Garland, Golbez, Exdeath).

Match videos: Replay Theater — Warrior of Light matches.

Builds

The Warrior of Light works with a wide variety of builds: balanced hybrids, Bravery Boost on Dodge, Side by Side. Since most of his damage comes from Dayflash assist combos and from his HP links, he is rarely built for bravery damage; high base bravery, on the other hand, benefits his assist combos enormously.

The documented hybrid build aims at EX intake and EX depletion — a good starting point, since most competitive builds play on damage, EX and/or gauge depletion. It rests on the Seal of Lufenia set (with the Equip Glitch, 450 CP in total): its DEF drop is offset by his very high base DEF, and Lufenian Dirk brings +1 ATK to counterbalance the low ATK of Heaven's Cloud, whose increased EX absorption range makes collecting EX Force easier. Assist: Sephiroth; summon: Rubicante.

Assist synergies

Warrior of Light as an assist

As an assist, the Warrior of Light is one of the weakest in the game (Low tier on the assist tier list). His bravery attacks do not hold the opponent for long and push them away from the player quickly; without an Assist Chase, he struggles to set up the player character's HP attacks and depends on Wall Rush. It is better to fight close to the ground so that Rising Buckler at least pins the opponent to the floor.

Rising Buckler keeps a niche: the best combination of vertical range and speed among aerial bravery assists, hence combos from certain chase moves (Laguna's Pummel, the close-range finisher of Kuja's Strike Energy) — even if Zidane's aerial BRV assist is generally preferred in that role. Shield of Light can block attacks, which is notable in a scramble and in checkmate situations, but as an HP attack it remains expensive and risky.

Recommended assists

  • Sephiroth — The most popular synergy in competition: combos from almost all his moves, a consistent Wall Rush, and multi-hits that make knockback cancels easy anywhere. His lower knockback angle makes Crossover > Rune Saber more consistent and more damaging as a follow-up.
  • Aerith — Less bravery damage and less whiff punishing, but safer combos and EX intake. Dayflash chase setups shine here (EX, bypassing LV2 Assist Change staggers), and Shield of Light after a Wall Rush allows a very damaging double assist with high base bravery.
  • Jecht — Strikes faster than Sephiroth; his aerial BRV opens extended ground combos for plenty of bravery, with the option of restarting through Dayflash's (ground) empty chase reset. A competent synergy, at the cost of consistent midscreen knockback cancels.

  • The solo combos section is marked “Main article pending”: only two solo combos and three assist combos (Sephiroth) are detailed.
  • The assist gain values of the moves are not filled in in the data.
  • The exact startup of the HP links (Rune Saber, Bitter End) is unknown (“?” in the tables), as are certain EX Force and Comrade's Vow counts for the combos (“???”).
  • Only one build is documented (the Seal of Lufenia hybrid); no variants are detailed (the dedicated builds article is not included in the data).
  • The community's empty chase record is undated (the solo combo record that accompanies it is dated December 2022): how current it is cannot be established.
